item.description: As Cop17 kicks off, records since 1921 show more bee species declining than increasing in all parts of Europe except the Alps Most of Europe’s wild bee species and about half of its hover fly species have declined over the last century, a study has found, as a UN biodiversity summit begins in Armenia. Records since 1921 show more bee species are declining than increasing in all parts of Europe except the Alpine region. The richness of bee and hover fly species suffered a persistent drop in the Atlantic and Continental regions, the study found, though trends in other regions were mixed or even… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. item.title: Cola de padres en las comisaría de Milán: 220 de los 271 retenidos por las protestas son menores
item.description: De las 271 personas que los agentes llevaron el domingo a la comisaría, 220 eran menores de edad, ocho de cada diez. De estos, 174 han dormido en la comisaría . item.description: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together. Fuente: BBC Sport.

item.title: Why are these lynxes washing their food?
item.description: Camera traps in Spain have captured a behavior never documented before in a wild cat: Iberian lynxes soaking their prey in water before eating it. Over five years, researchers recorded multiple females carrying dead rabbits to water troughs and repeatedly dunking them underwater. Scientists aren’t sure why. The behavior may help lynxes stay hydrated during […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Catalonia's former rebel president can return to Spain, court rules
item.description: The court upholds a decision to lift an arrest warrant for Carles Puigdemont linked to the independence bid he led in 2017. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: UEFA writes to FIFA demanding answers on Trump-Infantino dealings
item.description: European football chiefs have sent a list of 42 questions to FIFA, demanding answers about Gianni Infantino's alleged "conflicts of interest" over business dealings with the Trump family and the World Cup sell-off attempt. Fuente: Sky News - World.

item.title: France protests draw global attention: Trump, Vance blame immigration for unrest
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. Trump's post comes after similar comments made by Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. Vance, who is seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also drew a connection to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from the United States. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Macron kicks off three-day Gulf tour, seeks securing fuel supplies amid crisis
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday began a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs. Macron, just hours after slamming France's "unbridled" violence in an address late on Sunday, arrived in OPEC member Kuwait where he was welcomed by the emir, Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Drone attacks kill scores in Sudan's West Kordofan state and capital Khartoum
item.description: At least 80 people were killed in a drone strike near a market in Sudan’s southern West Kordofan state, a medical source and a witness said Monday, in one of the deadliest single attacks since the Sudan war erupted in 2023. A separate drone attack Monday in the capital Khartoum killed four, including three children. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: US midterms elections: Why data centers are becoming a key issue
item.description: With the US midterm elections just weeks away, data centers are emerging as a major political issue for both Republicans and Democrats. There are about 3,000 facilities currently operating in the country. With that number potentially doubling in the coming years, concern – and, in some cases, anger – is growing among voters. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson report from West Virginia. Fuente: France 24 - English.
